newsitem.title: USA: FBI offers new Olympic bomb witness sketch.
newsitem.headline: FBI offers new Olympic bomb witness sketch.

text.p: Agents investigating last year's Olympic bombing distributed a revised sketch of a possible witness on Friday, while an attorney announced plans to file a lawsuit against Olympic organisers and security firms on behalf of injured victims.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation issued a new drawing of someone seen sitting on the bench under which a bomb was placed in Atlanta's Centennial Olympic Park last July. The original drawing depicted a white male in his 20s with a goatee. He is clean-shaven in the new drawing.

"We've done another sketch and we've taken the goatee off," FBI agent Jack Daulton told Reuters. "The possibility exists that he didn't have a goatee three weeks before he was at the Olympic site, so somebody might not know him with a goatee."

Daulton, who heads the investigation into the Olympic bombing, said the man is not considered a suspect. Two witnesses saw him sitting on the bench between 12:40 a.m. and 12:45 a.m., minutes after the pipe bomb was placed underneath the bench and about 45 minutes before the bomb exploded.

Daulton said there is a "strong possibility" that the person or persons responsible for the Olympic bombing on July 27, 1996, was also responsible for bombs early this year at an abortion clinic and a gay nightclub in the Atlanta area.

Meanwhile, an attorney said he would file suit against the Atlanta Committee for the Olympic Games and two security firms on behalf of 15 people injured in the Olympic bombing, which killed two people and injured more than 100 others.
He said the lawsuit would claim that Olympic organisers realised the park was a potential target of a terrorist attack but failed to take precautions.

Federal agents are also still seeking someone seen in a videotape just before the bomb was placed in the park. "We have a very blurry figure sitting on the bench about 12:18 a.m.," Daulton said. "We can't make out a face. We can't make out facial features. We don't know who that person is, and we'd certainly like to know."

Daulton said a video tape received from the public shows a blurry object under the bench at 12:28 a.m. "We think there's a very good possibility that's the bomb," he said. "We have a still photograph taken between 12:30 a.m. and 12:40 a.m. that definitely shows the bomb underneath the bench."
"We continue to ask the public for photographs and videos. There were 70,000 people in the park. I truly believe that somebody has a photograph or a video" of the bomber, Daulton said.
